newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares at new record close, off highs.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares at new record close, off highs.

text.p: The market index at Istanbul's stock exchange closed at a new all-time high of 88,079.86 amid continued selective buying on Monday, but fell from day's highs on profit-taking, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 gained 1,095.93 points, or 1.26 percent from Friday and compared with Thursday's previous record close of 87,299.29. It brushed a high of 89,218 in afternoon trade.
Trade volume leapt to 26.24 trillion lira from 22.65 trillion on Friday.
The index had jumped 5.38 percent last week, toppling the stiff 85,000 barrier in the market's fourth attempt since late October.
"Technically, the market's first target is at one dollar and the second one at $1.3," said Resat Kutucular from Toros securities.
In dollar terms, the index stood at $0.88 on Monday, compared to a $1 record on April 8 and $0.67 at end-1995.
"Last week's rise was very important because the index posted real gains in dollar terms which meant that the direction turned upward in the medium term," Kutucular said.
Some brokers said positive developments on the economic front, particularly progress in privatisation, might be needed to fuel market expectations to support the uptrend.

Of the 231 shares traded, 90 advanced, 80 declined and 61 closed unchanged. The 85-share industrial index firmed 0.59 percent to 92,733.98 and the 15-share financial index jumped 2.76 percent to 85,908.04.

Actives were led by utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira at 105,000, T.Isbank's C series shares, up 1,000 lira at 17,250, Koc Holding, up 750 lira at 21,000 and Kepez Elektrik, up 4,500 lira at 102,500.
Turnover in the most heavily traded four stocks made up 34.7 percent of the total volume.
